text: Welcome to FBDI and ADFdi. This course opens the Data Loading and Integrations stage of your Oracle Fusion Financials path. You've used SQL to pull data out of Oracle Fusion. Now we look at how data gets in — one record at a time, or fifty thousand at a time.

There are four common doors into Oracle Fusion. Manual entry: a user types one record into a page. File-Based Data Import, or FBDI: spreadsheet templates turned into CSV files and run through an import process built for huge volumes. ADF Desktop Integration, or ADFdi: an Excel add-in that talks directly to a live Fusion page. And REST APIs: external systems calling Oracle Fusion's web services directly, with no spreadsheet at all.

The choice isn't personal preference. It comes down to three questions. How many rows — a handful favors manual entry, thousands favor FBDI. How often — a one-time conversion favors FBDI, a recurring unattended feed favors a REST API integration. And who's doing the work — a finance power user with Excel can run ADFdi or FBDI with no coding at all.

FBDI and ADFdi solve the same problem in different ways. FBDI stages data through interface tables in two separate steps, which is built for very large volumes and one-time conversions. ADFdi skips most of that staging and talks to the live page through Excel, which suits smaller, interactive batches where you want to see and fix problems as you go.

Both tools exist because Fusion's web pages were never meant to have a thousand rows pasted into them by hand. They're the supported way around that. Up next, lesson two: what File-Based Data Import actually is, and when it's the right tool for the job.
